facts.statement: Pawpawsaurus is a nodosaurid ankylosaur from the late Albian of Tarrant County, Texas, whose name means "Pawpaw Lizard".
facts.quote: Pawpawsaurus, meaning "Pawpaw Lizard", is a nodosaurid ankylosaur from the Cretaceous (late Albian) of Tarrant County, Texas, discovered in May 1992.

facts.statement: The fossil of Pawpawsaurus was discovered in May 1992.
facts.quote: discovered in May 1992

facts.statement: Cameron Campbell discovered Pawpawsaurus in the Paw Paw Formation, Tarrant County, Texas, in May 1992.
facts.quote: Pawpawsaurus was found in the Paw Paw Formation in Tarrant County, Texas, in May 1992, by Cameron Campbell.

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Pawpawsaurus is a complete skull (SMU 73203) lacking mandibles, which was used to name the species Pawpawsaurus campbelli.
facts.quote: A complete skull, SMU 73203, is the only specimen, from which the binomial was named Pawpawsaurus campbelli.

facts.statement: Pawpawsaurus was formally described by Y. N. Lee in 1996.
facts.quote: descrito por Y. N. Lee en 1996

facts.statement: Pawpawsaurus lived during the middle Cretaceous, approximately 111 to 99 million years ago, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 111 y 99 millones de años, en el Albiense, en lo que es hoy Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Pawpawsaurus lived during the Albian stage, from 106.3 to 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (106.3 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Pawpawsaurus was a medium-sized nodosaur measuring 4.5 meters in length.
facts.quote: Pawpawsaurus was a medium-sized nodosaur measuring 4.5 m long.

facts.statement: Based on skull dimensions, Pawpawsaurus is estimated to have been about 4.5 meters long, 1.5 meters high, and weighing one ton.
facts.quote: Según las dimensiones del cráneo, se cree que Pawpawsaurus medía aproximadamente 4,5 metros de largo, 1.5 de alto y una tonelada de peso.

facts.statement: Pawpawsaurus is the only known nodosaurid to possess bony eyelids, a feature common in ankylosaurids.
facts.quote: This is the only nodosaurid known to have possessed the bony eyelids commonly found in ankylosaurids.

facts.statement: The skull of Pawpawsaurus ended in a horny beak and featured a unique model of skin plates above the cranium.
facts.quote: El cráneo tiene el tabique incompleto y ningún paladar secundario sin faltarle ninguna pieza, terminaba en un pico córneo y un modelo único de placas cutáneas encima del cráneo.

facts.statement: A 2016 study used CT scans on the complete skull of Pawpawsaurus to reconstruct its brain, nasal cavities, and inner ear.
facts.quote: The skull is complete enough for a 2016 study to be able to identify and reconstruct the brain, nasal cavities and inner ear of the specimen, and CT scan it to find new anatomical features.

facts.statement: The brain of Pawpawsaurus measured 96 mm in length and 35 mm in width.
facts.quote: The brain of Pawpawsaurus is 96 mm long and 35 mm wide.

facts.statement: CT scans revealed that Pawpawsaurus had relatively poor hearing, comparable to that of modern crocodilians.
facts.quote: CT scans of its skull and brain by Paulina-Carabajal and Louis Jacobs et al. revealed that Pawpawsaurus hearing was on par with that of modern crocodilians, indicating that its hearing was relatively poor.

facts.statement: Pawpawsaurus had a sense of smell more powerful and acute than many contemporary theropods due to its large nasal cavities.
facts.quote: Its sense of smell meanwhile, while not as advanced as that of later ankylosaurs, was still more powerful and acute than many of the theropods existent at the time thanks to its large nasal cavities.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the enlarged nasal cavities of Pawpawsaurus may have helped cool blood entering the brain, locate food and mates, or detect danger.
facts.quote: Las cavidades nasales agrandadas de Pawpawsaurus probablemente también habrían sido útiles para enfriar la sangre que ingresaba al cerebro, encontrar comida y posibles parejas, o alertarlo sobre un peligro.

facts.statement: The genus Texasetes, found in the Paw Paw Formation, may prove to be a junior synonym of Pawpawsaurus.
facts.quote: La Formación Paw Paw ha producido otro nodosáurido, Texasetes (Coombs, 1995), que puede resultar siendo un sinónimo más moderno de Pawpawsaurus.

facts.statement: Vickaryous et al. (2004) proposed that Pawpawsaurus forms a basal polytomy with Sauropelta and Silvisaurus nested deep to Cedarpelta.
facts.quote: Vickaryous et al. (2004) have stated that "Sauropelta edwardsorum, Silvisaurus condrayi, and Pawpawsaurus campbelli form a basal polytomy nested deep to Cedarpelta."

facts.statement: A 2018 analysis by Rivera-Sylva and colleagues placed Pawpawsaurus within the clade Struthiosaurini as a relative of Struthiosaurus.
facts.quote: Alternatively, Pawpawsaurus has been identified as a relative of Struthiosaurus, with cladogram below showing the results of the 2018 phylogenetic analysis of Rivera-Sylva and colleagues, resolving Pawpawsaurus within the clade Struthiosaurini as labelled by Madzia et al., with relationships outside Struthiosaurini excluded for simplicity.

facts.statement: A 2017 analysis by Brown et al. placed Pawpawsaurus in a clade with Borealopelta and Europelta.
facts.quote: However, the strict consensus tree of a phylogenetic analysis performed by Brown et al. (2017) placed Pawpawsaurus in a clade with Borealopelta markmitchelli and Europelta carbonensis.

rejected.statement: The inner ear of Pawpawsaurus was 27 mm tall and 15.5 mm wide at the level of the semicircular canals.
rejected.quote: The inner ear is also similar to ankylosaurians to the exclusion of Kunbarrasaurus, being 27 mm tall and 15.5 mm wide at the level of the semicircular canals.
